logicalBugs.explanation: A failed voucher Save can still persist part of the edit: a new name or discount type can survive a rejected channel discount, and deleting an existing code can succeed while its duplicate replacement is rejected. Returning to the list and choosing Ignore changes does not undo those already committed edits.

rootCause.explanation: createUpdateHandler starts voucherUpdate, voucherChannelListingUpdate, code deletion and catalogue updates as independent promises and waits for Promise.all only after they have started. Errors are collected after independent commits, without a transaction, preflight barrier or compensation. The same orchestration produces metadata/channel partial writes and code replacement partial deletion; type changes can also race channel validation against the old discount type.

analysis.explanation: The detail save runs updateVoucher and updateChannels independently in Promise.all. The voucher type/name can commit while channel amount validation fails, and type changes do not revalidate existing channel values as one atomic mutation.

The detail update starts voucherUpdate and voucherCodesDelete independently in the requests array; deletion commits even if adding the replacement code fails. No transaction or compensation spans the calls.

logicalBugs.explanation: Voucher Save can report "Voucher updated" while retaining a false unsaved draft and leave-page warning. Reload shows the stored canonical settings and clears the warning.

rootCause.explanation: The detail form uses useForm with useStateFromProps and its merge function. That merge replaces a local field only when the incoming initial field differs from its previous server value. Saving a normalized value that is unchanged on the server therefore retains the changed local toggle/text, including disabled fields, zero-requirement selections and blank defaulted dates. No successful-save reset reconciles the whole form with canonical persisted values.

analysis.explanation: The submit handler clears inactive discount drafts and converts zero requirements/disabled values to server representations, but the form dirty comparison still contains the original local toggles/values and compares them to newly derived server initial data. Those unsaved local representations are not reconciled on success.

The form is initialized from split saved DateTimes but keeps changed local fields through prop reconciliation; normalized mutation/refetch values are not explicitly reset into the native date/time draft after submission.

logicalBugs.explanation: On a saved voucher, Save remains available for a zero minimum item quantity or zero total usage limit even while the field displays "Enter at least 1 item" or "Enter a limit of at least 1". Saving can report success, clear an existing quantity requirement, or store a zero cap that reopens as disabled.

rootCause.explanation: VoucherRequirements and VoucherLimits calculate invalid minimum quantity/usage-limit flags only for inline display. The shared createVoucherUpdateHandler gates submit using validateChannelListing and buildChannelListingLocalErrors, which contain neither of those non-channel checks. Consequently those displayed invalid fields reach the same submit path as valid data.

analysis.explanation: VoucherLimits derives hasInvalidUsageLimit for display only, while the save path submits hasUsageLimit/usageLimit without using that validation to stop the request; zero is then interpreted as an absent cap in display logic.

VoucherRequirements displays an error for a value below one but the submit handler does not stop on that UI-only condition; it forwards zero, which means no item requirement, and other independent successful updates can produce a success acknowledgement.

Replace the limit with 0. Observe “Enter a limit of at least 1.” and click Save.
Reload the saved voucher. Observe the limit toggle off and its input hidden; the saved voucher response still contains usageLimit 0.

logicalBugs.explanation: Voucher minimum item quantity and total usage limit accept fractional values such as 1.5 or 7.5 without an integer validation message. Save can silently truncate the displayed quantity/cap to an integer, while an existing voucher’s edited cap can remain displayed as a fractional number of redemptions.

rootCause.explanation: The quantity and usage-limit number controls validate minimum/range conditions but do not enforce Number.isInteger or an equivalent integer-domain input contract before submit. Handlers forward parseFloat quantity and numeric usage-limit values to integer API/model fields; detail state/display can retain the submitted fraction while creation/storage normalizes it. These are the same missing integer-domain validation exposed through distinct create/edit fields.

analysis.explanation: Number fields lack an integer constraint, and handlers submit parseFloat quantity/numeric usage limits into integer GraphQL/model fields. Neither path reports the lossy integer coercion to the user.

The usage-limit input accepts decimal values without an integer check; detail mutation/cache reconciliation retains the submitted numeric cap for uses-left/redemption arithmetic instead of validating/reloading an integer representation.

reproductionPaths.explanation: The integer minimum-item quantity field accepts a visible 1.5 and reports a successful Save, but silently stores 1. The form should visibly filter out the decimal point while typing or reject the fractional value on Save; successful saving should preserve the displayed accepted quantity.

sourceBugs.name: Fractional minimum quantity silently truncates on save

reproductionPaths.expected: The form should either strip the decimal point while typing so 1.5 visibly becomes 15 before Save and saves as 15, or reject the fractional value on Save. A successful Save must preserve the displayed accepted quantity.
reproductionPaths.actual: The field displays 1.5. Save shows “Voucher updated” and changes the quantity to 1 without a validation message; the saved quantity remains 1 after reload.

Click Save. Observe “Voucher updated” and the quantity changing to 1.
Reload the voucher and reopen Requirements. Observe that Minimum quantity of items remains enabled with the stored value 1.

logicalBugs.explanation: Leaving a voucher detail page open across its start or end time does not update the displayed schedule/availability status. A scheduled voucher can remain Scheduled after it starts, or an ended voucher can remain Active until another refresh/render occurs.

rootCause.explanation: getVoucherSchedulePhase evaluates Date.now only when React renders. No timer/subscription schedules a render at start/end, so status remains stale on an otherwise idle page.

reproductionPaths.explanation: On an open voucher detail page, the header status, the Schedule card label and the channel dot do not change when the scheduled start or end time passes. After the start time it still said "Scheduled · in 2 minutes". After the end time it still said Active, with a green Channel-USD dot. Refreshing the page shows the correct phase each time.

sourceBugs.name: Open voucher detail page keeps stale schedule status after start and end times pass

reproductionPaths.expected: While the page stays open, the header status, Schedule card label and channel indicator change from Scheduled to Active to Inactive/Ended as the start and end times pass, matching what a refresh shows.
reproductionPaths.actual: Start was 02:49 and end was 02:51 EDT on Oct 28 2026. At 02:49:12 and again at 02:49:54 the page still showed "Scheduled · in 2 minutes", and the Schedule card still said Scheduled. A refresh at 02:50:05 showed Active. At 02:51:30, after the end time, the page still showed Active with a green Channel-USD dot. Refreshing then showed "Inactive · 1 minute ago", "Ended" and a grey channel dot.
reproSteps: Sign in as the vouchers admin (saved session) with browser timezone America/New_York, then open /discounts/vouchers/add
Name: voucher-schedule-mo1. Add a manual code SCHEDMO1. Under Availability > Manage, assign Channel-USD. Set the Channel-USD percentage to 5.

Set Start Date to 10/28/2026 and Start Hour to 02:49 AM (about 3 minutes ahead). Check Set end date and set End Date to 10/28/2026 and End Hour to 02:51 AM. Click Save; the toast says 'Voucher created' and the header shows 'Scheduled · in 2 minutes'.
Leave the page open past 02:49. At 02:49:54 the header still shows 'Scheduled · in 2 minutes'.
Refresh at 02:50: the header shows Active and the Channel-USD dot is green.
Leave the page open past 02:51. At 02:51:30 it still shows Active with a green Channel-USD dot. Refreshing shows 'Inactive · 1 minute ago' and Ended.
